# System Design Primer (enterprise fork)

> Enterprise-augmented fork of Donne Martin's System Design Primer (CC BY 4.0). Original study guide preserved; guides, pattern cards, templates, and skills cover production systems.

Generated by scripts/build_catalog.py. Do not edit by hand. The file list follows the llms.txt convention at https://llmstxt.org/.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): How a coding agent should use this repo and which files to load.
- [README.md](README.md): Fork landing page, then the original System Design Primer study guide.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): Pull-request conventions, frontmatter, and how to regenerate the catalog.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): Notable changes to this fork.
- [catalog.json](catalog.json): Machine-readable index of every catalogued doc (schema version 2).
- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): Index of the full-text bundles under llms-full/.

## Skills pack

- [Enterprise system design skills](pack/README.md): Tool-agnostic architect, threat-modeler, cost-estimator, design-reviewer, and ADR-writer skills, with the references and worked example they ship with.
- [Complementary sources](pack/corpora/INDEX.md): License-checked index of outside sources, grouped by whether this repo may copy them, must share-alike, or may only link.
- [adr-writer](pack/skills/adr-writer/SKILL.md): Use this when recording an architecture decision: context, the decision, alternatives rejected and why, consequences, and status, as an Architecture Decision Record.
- [When to write an ADR](pack/skills/adr-writer/reference/when-to-write.md): Choose an ADR to record one decision already made, an RFC while several teams still have to critique an open choice, and a design doc for the whole system.
- [ADR template](pack/skills/adr-writer/template.md): The canonical Architecture Decision Record outline: status, context, the decision, rejected alternatives, and consequences.
- [cost-estimator](pack/skills/cost-estimator/SKILL.md): Use this when turning a system design into a cost estimate: workload drivers, unit costs labeled as assumptions, formulas before totals, sensitivity, and unit economics.
- [Cost estimate method](pack/skills/cost-estimator/reference/method.md): Formulas for a design cost estimate, then a worked object-storage example with every product shown.
- [design-reviewer](pack/skills/design-reviewer/SKILL.md): Use this when reviewing a proposed software architecture or system design for production gaps: single points of failure, cache invalidation, consistency, 10x load, failure modes, authentication and authorization, OWASP ASVS, compliance, observability, retention, cost, migration, and team boundaries.
- [Design review checklist](pack/skills/design-reviewer/checklist.md): Ordered review questions from single points of failure through ownership, plus the ASVS 5.0.0 chapter names used as citations.
- [system-architect](pack/skills/system-architect/SKILL.md): Use this when turning a feature or product request into an enterprise system design: functional and non-functional requirements, back-of-the-envelope traffic, storage, and bandwidth estimates, a mermaid component sketch, a data model, an API outline, and explicit tradeoffs.
- [Design method](pack/skills/system-architect/reference/approach.md): The four-step design method adapted from the Primer, and the section headings a written design has to emit.
- [Data, consistency, and availability](pack/skills/system-architect/reference/data.md): How to pick a store, a consistency model, and a replication scheme, with the Primer's older terms mapped to current names.
- [Enterprise checks for a design](pack/skills/system-architect/reference/enterprise-checks.md): Production decisions the architect writes as requirements before the sketch, covering identity, tenancy, retention, operability, cost, and migration.
- [Estimates](pack/skills/system-architect/reference/estimates.md): Back-of-the-envelope formulas plus the Primer's powers-of-two, latency, and availability figures used for capacity math.
- [Scaling patterns](pack/skills/system-architect/reference/scalability.md): When cache, shard, CDN, queue, and load-balancing patterns apply, including Primer notes that no longer match current practice.
- [threat-modeler](pack/skills/threat-modeler/SKILL.md): Use this when turning a data-flow description into a STRIDE threat model: one row per element or trust boundary, with severity and a mitigation or an accepted risk.
- [AI threat prompts](pack/skills/threat-modeler/reference/ai-threats.md): Extra abuses to walk when a design calls a model, retrieves untrusted text, or lets a model invoke tools.
- [STRIDE reference](pack/skills/threat-modeler/reference/stride.md): Six questions to ask of each element and each trust-boundary crossing, plus the severity scale the threat-modeler skill uses.

## Enterprise guide

- [Enterprise guide](enterprise/README.md): Production topics the System Design Primer does not cover, split into short decision-oriented pages.
- [What's dated in the Primer](enterprise/whats-dated.md): Where the System Design Primer's advice shows its era, and the current equivalent to use in a design.

## Identity

- [Authorization engines](enterprise/identity/authorization-engines.md): Keep simple RBAC in the service that owns the row, and add a relationship or policy engine when many services must answer the same graph or the same policy.
- [Authorization models](enterprise/identity/authorization-models.md): Choose RBAC, ABAC, or ReBAC for the decision, and enforce it on the server from the authenticated identity.
- [OIDC and OAuth 2.0](enterprise/identity/oidc-oauth2.md): Pick an OAuth 2.0 flow, bind tokens to the right audience, and treat OpenID Connect as the identity layer on top.
- [Passkeys and MFA](enterprise/identity/passkeys-mfa.md): Prefer phishing-resistant authenticators, treat recovery as part of the factor, and require the IdP to carry the assurance level you claim.
- [SSO and SAML](enterprise/identity/saml-sso.md): Accept enterprise single sign-on through SAML 2.0 when a customer IdP requires it, and keep the assertion checks strict.
- [SCIM provisioning](enterprise/identity/scim-provisioning.md): Push user and group lifecycle from the IdP with SCIM 2.0, and treat deprovision as disable-now plus a separate delete decision.
- [Secrets management](enterprise/identity/secrets.md): Keep secrets in a manager, inject them at runtime, scope who can read them, and rotate them without a redeploy heroics story.
- [Service-to-service auth](enterprise/identity/service-to-service.md): Give every workload an identity and a short-lived credential, using workload identity, SPIFFE, or mutually authenticated TLS.

## Security

- [Encryption and key management](enterprise/security/encryption-keys.md): Encrypt in transit and at rest with managed keys, separate data keys from key-encryption keys, and do not invent a cipher.
- [OWASP ASVS chapter map](enterprise/security/owasp-asvs.md): Point a design at the ASVS 5.0.0 chapter that covers the control, without copying the standard's requirement text.
- [Post-quantum migration](enterprise/security/post-quantum.md): Inventory where classical public-key crypto protects long-lived data, prefer hybrid key agreement first, and treat NIST's 2030 and 2035 dates as a draft timeline until IR 8547 is final.
- [Software supply chain](enterprise/security/supply-chain.md): Know what you build, produce an SBOM, sign the artifact, and deploy only what you verified.
- [Threat modeling with STRIDE](enterprise/security/threat-modeling.md): Walk the data flows once per trust boundary and name spoofing, tampering, repudiation, disclosure, denial of service, and elevation of privilege.
- [Zero trust](enterprise/security/zero-trust.md): Authenticate and authorize every request, and treat network location as an untrusted hint.

## Tenancy

- [Per-tenant data and keys](enterprise/tenancy/data-and-keys.md): Put the tenant on every record and decide which tenants get their own encryption key.
- [Tenant isolation models](enterprise/tenancy/isolation-models.md): Pick silo, pool, or bridge isolation per tier of tenant, and write down what a bug in one model can leak.
- [Tenant onboarding and offboarding](enterprise/tenancy/lifecycle.md): Provision a tenant as a record plus policy, and offboard it including access, exports, deletion, and backups.
- [Noisy neighbors](enterprise/tenancy/noisy-neighbor.md): Cap one tenant's load so a shared pool stays fair, and move a tenant to a silo when caps are not enough.
- [Tenant-aware routing](enterprise/tenancy/routing.md): Resolve the tenant from the credential and the host, then send the request to that tenant's home region or cell.

## Compliance

- [Tamper-evident audit logs](enterprise/compliance/audit-logs.md): Record privileged actions in an append-only log that operators cannot quietly edit, and keep it separate from debug logs.
- [EU regulations for engineering](enterprise/compliance/eu-regulations.md): Map the AI Act, DORA, NIS2, and the Cyber Resilience Act to logs, inventories, incident clocks, and tests, and separate adopted dates from the original calendar.
- [HIPAA and PCI DSS basics](enterprise/compliance/hipaa-pci.md): Shrink the systems that touch PHI or cardholder data, and put the extra controls only on what remains.
- [ISO 27001 and FedRAMP](enterprise/compliance/iso27001-fedramp.md): Treat ISO/IEC 27001:2022 as an ISMS with a statement of applicability, and treat FedRAMP as an authorization boundary with evidence that keeps moving.
- [GDPR and CCPA basics](enterprise/compliance/privacy.md): Inventory personal data, minimize it, and build export and deletion as product paths rather than as tickets.
- [Data residency](enterprise/compliance/residency.md): Pin a tenant's data, backups, and operator access to the regions the contract allows.
- [Retention and deletion](enterprise/compliance/retention.md): Give every store a retention period and a deletion path that includes indexes, vendors, and backups.
- [SOC 2 basics](enterprise/compliance/soc2.md): Treat SOC 2 as an attestation that named controls operated over a period, and build the evidence those controls need.

## Reliability

- [Cell-based architecture](enterprise/reliability/cell-based-architecture.md): Bound blast radius with full-stack cells, a thin router, and shuffle sharding where a shared pool is still required.
- [Chaos testing](enterprise/reliability/chaos.md): Run a small, reversible fault with a hypothesis and an abort switch, and write down what broke.
- [Circuit breakers and bulkheads](enterprise/reliability/circuit-breaker-bulkhead.md): Stop calling a dependency that is failing, and isolate its concurrency so it cannot sink the whole process.
- [Disaster recovery, RPO, and RTO](enterprise/reliability/disaster-recovery.md): Name how much data you can lose and how fast you must be back, then test the restore that those numbers require.
- [Load shedding](enterprise/reliability/load-shedding.md): Reject excess work early, with a clear retry signal, before the process collapses under queueing delay.
- [Multi-region architectures](enterprise/reliability/multi-region.md): Choose active-passive or active-active from the RPO, the RTO, and whether two regions may write the same key.
- [Retries, backoff, and timeouts](enterprise/reliability/retries-timeouts.md): Bound every remote call with a timeout, and retry only idempotent work with jittered backoff.

## Observability

- [Alerting and on-call](enterprise/observability/alerting-oncall.md): Page a named owner on user-visible symptoms that threaten the error budget, and keep a human rotation that can act.
- [Incident response](enterprise/observability/incidents.md): Declare early, assign roles, mitigate first, and keep a timeline that the postmortem can trust.
- [OpenTelemetry](enterprise/observability/opentelemetry.md): Instrument with OpenTelemetry and put sampling, redaction, and vendor export in the collector, not in application code.
- [Blameless postmortems](enterprise/observability/postmortems.md): Write what happened, why the system allowed it, and which actions will change the system, without blaming a person.
- [SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets](enterprise/observability/slos.md): Define a user-visible indicator, set a target over a window, and spend the error budget on purpose.
- [Logs, metrics, and traces](enterprise/observability/telemetry.md): Use metrics for symptoms and alerts, traces for one request's path, and logs for the detail you cannot aggregate.

## Data

- [Caching at scale](enterprise/data/caching-at-scale.md): Place cache tiers, stop stampedes and hot keys, and size a shared cache without pretending it is the database.
- [Change data capture](enterprise/data/cdc.md): Stream committed database changes from the log when consumers need the row-level history the database already committed.
- [Event-driven architecture](enterprise/data/event-driven.md): Publish facts that already happened, let consumers build their own state, and treat delivery as at-least-once.
- [Data governance](enterprise/data/governance.md): Assign an owner, a classification, a lineage, and an access rule to data people will rely on.
- [Idempotency](enterprise/data/idempotency.md): Make a retried request return the original result, and reject the same key when the body differs.
- [Sagas](enterprise/data/sagas.md): Split a multi-service business transaction into local steps plus compensations, and choose a choreography or an orchestrator.
- [Schema evolution](enterprise/data/schema-evolution.md): Change events and tables so old and new producers and consumers overlap for at least one release.
- [Search](enterprise/data/search.md): Run lexical search, vector search, or both as a rebuildable projection, with tenant filters and a ranking eval you can recompute.
- [Transactional outbox](enterprise/data/transactional-outbox.md): Write the business change and the message you must publish in the same database transaction, then publish asynchronously.
- [Warehouse and lakehouse](enterprise/data/warehouse-lakehouse.md): Keep operational stores for transactions, and land analytical copies in a warehouse or a table format on object storage.
- [Workflow engines](enterprise/data/workflow-engines.md): Choose durable execution, an orchestrated saga, choreography, a job queue, or cron from how long the process lives and who must remember the step.

## APIs

- [Contract testing](enterprise/apis/contract-testing.md): Check producer and consumer agreements in CI so a shared staging environment is not the only integration test.
- [Errors, pagination, and async operations](enterprise/apis/errors-pagination-async.md): Return problem details with a stable type, page with opaque cursors, and point long work at a status resource.
- [API gateways](enterprise/apis/gateways.md): Put edge concerns at the gateway and keep product policy in the service that owns the data.
- [Rate limiting](enterprise/apis/rate-limiting.md): Choose a limiter algorithm from whether bursts are allowed, and key it on the identity that should pay the cost.
- [Realtime delivery](enterprise/apis/realtime.md): Choose a connection style, fan out through gateways, and size memory and outbound messages per node.
- [REST, gRPC, and GraphQL](enterprise/apis/styles.md): Pick one style per boundary from who the caller is, whether the shape is stable, and who pays for round trips.
- [API versioning](enterprise/apis/versioning.md): Evolve contracts compatibly, and introduce an explicit version only when a break is unavoidable.
- [Webhooks](enterprise/apis/webhooks.md): Sign each delivery, retry with backoff, and make the receiver dedupe on an event id.

## Delivery

- [CI and CD](enterprise/delivery/cicd.md): Build an artifact once, test it, sign it, and promote that same digest through environments.
- [Database migrations and rollback](enterprise/delivery/database-migrations.md): Change schemas in expand and contract steps so the previous application version still runs, and so rollback does not require time travel.
- [Feature flags](enterprise/delivery/feature-flags.md): Separate release from deploy with short-lived flags, and make the off state safe when the flag service is down.
- [Infrastructure as code and environments](enterprise/delivery/iac-environments.md): Describe infrastructure in reviewed code, and keep environments separated without copying production personal data downhill.
- [Production readiness](enterprise/delivery/production-readiness.md): Gate a service on ownership, SLOs, failure modes, restore, and rollback before it is allowed to take tier-1 traffic.
- [Progressive delivery](enterprise/delivery/progressive-delivery.md): Expose a release to a small slice first, watch the SLO, and expand or roll back on that evidence.
- [Testing strategy](enterprise/delivery/testing-strategy.md): Keep a portfolio of fast tests, a thin end-to-end slice, and load tests whose pass line is the SLO, including the queueing an open workload exposes.

## Cost

- [Cost allocation](enterprise/cost/allocation.md): Attribute shared spend to teams and tenants with tags and a written split, so showback is explainable.
- [Capacity planning](enterprise/cost/capacity.md): Turn the traffic estimate into a resource plan with headroom, a lead time, and a date to revisit.
- [FinOps](enterprise/cost/finops.md): Make spend visible to the teams who cause it, and review it on a cadence with the same seriousness as an SLO.
- [Unit economics](enterprise/cost/unit-economics.md): Express cost per business unit so a design change can be compared to the revenue or the budget it serves.

## Organization

- [Build versus buy](enterprise/organization/build-vs-buy.md): Score differentiation, total cost, time, skill, vendor risk, compliance, and the exit, then revisit the score at renewal.
- [Conway's law](enterprise/organization/conways-law.md): Expect the system to mirror team communication, and change the team boundary when you want a different system boundary.
- [ADRs and RFCs](enterprise/organization/decisions.md): Use an RFC to shape a proposal with the people it affects, and an ADR to record the decision you actually made.
- [Software delivery metrics](enterprise/organization/delivery-metrics.md): Measure DORA's five software delivery metrics from deploys and incidents, and pair them with SLOs so speed is not the only score.
- [Service ownership](enterprise/organization/ownership.md): Give every service and store one owning team that ships it, runs it, and answers for its data.
- [Platform teams](enterprise/organization/platform-teams.md): Run an internal platform as a product with customers, a golden path, and a support model that is not a ticket black hole.
- [Team topologies](enterprise/organization/team-topologies.md): Organize teams by the kind of work they do and the way they are allowed to interact, so delivery is not an accident of the org chart.

## Modernization

- [Anti-corruption layer](enterprise/modernization/anti-corruption-layer.md): Translate between a legacy model and a new model in one place, so the new model does not grow the legacy system's concepts.
- [Modular monolith](enterprise/modernization/modular-monolith.md): Keep one deployable, split it into modules with hard boundaries, and extract a service only when a team or a scale number requires it.
- [Strangler fig](enterprise/modernization/strangler-fig.md): Put a seam in front of the legacy system and replace one capability at a time until the old path can be deleted.

## AI

- [AI systems](enterprise/ai/README.md): How to put a model behind a gateway, ground it with retrieval, constrain tools, and score the result.
- [Agents and tools](enterprise/ai/agents-and-tools.md): Let an agent call tools only with the user's scoped credentials, a budget, and an audit record.
- [Evals and observability](enterprise/ai/evals-and-observability.md): Score model and retrieval changes on versioned sets, and trace them with OpenTelemetry GenAI attributes that are still Development status.
- [LLM application architecture](enterprise/ai/llm-app-architecture.md): Put a gateway in front of model providers, and bound cost, latency, failover, and what data leaves the tenant.
- [LLM security](enterprise/ai/llm-security.md): Treat model input and output as untrusted, and map the failures you build for to the OWASP GenAI lists by id.
- [Retrieval-augmented generation](enterprise/ai/rag.md): Index tenant documents into chunks and embeddings, retrieve with filters and hybrid search, and delete every copy.

## Reference architectures

- [Reference architectures](enterprise/reference-architectures/README.md): Five end-to-end designs with requirements, estimates, a diagram, tradeoffs, and a severity-ranked design review.
- [Reference architecture: data platform](enterprise/reference-architectures/data-platform.md): CDC from operational databases into a lakehouse with owned curated tables, deletion, and a catalog.
- [Reference architecture: event-driven orders and payments](enterprise/reference-architectures/event-driven-orders.md): Checkout as an orchestrated saga: authorize payment, reserve inventory, then capture, with an outbox and idempotent provider calls.
- [Reference architecture: internal platform with SSO and audit](enterprise/reference-architectures/internal-platform.md): An internal developer platform with corporate SSO, a service catalog, and a tamper-evident audit log.
- [Reference architecture: multi-tenant B2B SaaS](enterprise/reference-architectures/multi-tenant-b2b-saas.md): A pooled work-management SaaS with a bridge tier for large tenants, SSO, and tenant-scoped webhooks.
- [Reference architecture: multi-tenant RAG assistant](enterprise/reference-architectures/rag-assistant.md): A pooled B2B assistant that answers from each tenant's documents, with filtered hybrid retrieval and a deletion path.

## Pattern cards

- [Pattern cards](patterns/README.md): One card per pattern with the problem, when to use it, when not to, tradeoffs, and failure modes.
- [Anti-corruption layer](patterns/anti-corruption-layer.md): Translate between a new model and a legacy or external model so foreign concepts stay at the edge.
- [API gateway](patterns/api-gateway.md): A single edge that authenticates, limits, and routes requests, without owning product decisions.
- [Availability and failover](patterns/availability-failover.md): Stand up a second copy and a tested promotion path so one failure does not end the service.
- [Backend for frontend](patterns/backend-for-frontend.md): A server-side API shaped for one client, aggregating downstream services so the client does not.
- [Blue/green](patterns/blue-green.md): Run two complete environments and switch traffic from the live color to the idle one.
- [Bulkhead](patterns/bulkhead.md): Give each dependency or tenant a separate concurrency limit so one failure cannot take every thread.
- [Cache-aside](patterns/cache-aside.md): The application reads the cache, and on a miss loads the store and fills the cache.
- [Cache invalidation](patterns/cache-invalidation.md): Define who may overwrite or delete a cached entry and the maximum staleness a caller can observe.
- [Canary](patterns/canary.md): Send a small fraction of traffic to the new version and expand only if the user-visible metrics hold.
- [Change data capture](patterns/cdc.md): Read committed row changes from the database log and stream them to other systems.
- [Content delivery network](patterns/cdn.md): Serve cacheable bytes from a location near the user so the origin does not see that request.
- [Cell-based architecture](patterns/cell-based-architecture.md): Run the workload as several full stacks, each serving a slice of tenants, so one failure does not take the product down.
- [Circuit breaker](patterns/circuit-breaker.md): Stop calling a dependency that is failing, fail fast for a cool-down, then try a few probes.
- [Consistency patterns](patterns/consistency-patterns.md): Choose weak, eventual, or strong consistency per path, and write the partition behavior separately from the healthy-path latency.
- [CQRS](patterns/cqrs.md): Use a write model shaped for commands and a read model shaped for queries, updated asynchronously.
- [Denormalization](patterns/denormalization.md): Store a copy of a field next to the data that reads it, so a hot path does not join.
- [Durable workflow](patterns/durable-workflow.md): Record each step of a long-running process in an event history and continue by replaying that history, instead of holding the work in memory.
- [Event sourcing](patterns/event-sourcing.md): Store the state of an aggregate as an append-only sequence of domain events and derive current state by fold.
- [Feature flags](patterns/feature-flags.md): Branch behavior at runtime so you can ship code dark, open it gradually, or turn it off without a redeploy.
- [Federation](patterns/federation.md): Split databases by function so each domain has its own store and its own write path.
- [Idempotency keys](patterns/idempotency-keys.md): Store the result of a write under a client-supplied key so a retry returns the same result and does not repeat the effect.
- [Load balancing](patterns/load-balancing.md): Spread requests across healthy targets so one instance is not the user-facing capacity or the single failure.
- [Load shedding](patterns/load-shedding.md): Reject new work when the service is past a defined saturation point so accepted work can finish.
- [Message queues and async processing](patterns/message-queues.md): Accept work onto a durable queue and let a worker finish it after the user request returns.
- [Rate limiting](patterns/rate-limiting.md): Count or meter requests per identity and reject the excess before the service is overloaded.
- [Refresh-ahead](patterns/refresh-ahead.md): The cache reloads a hot entry before its TTL expires so the next reader does not pay for a miss.
- [Leader-follower replication](patterns/replication-leader-follower.md): One leader accepts writes and replicates them to followers that serve reads.
- [Multi-leader replication](patterns/replication-multi-leader.md): More than one node accepts writes, and the nodes converge, with conflicts when they write the same key.
- [Retry with backoff](patterns/retry-with-backoff.md): Repeat a failed idempotent call with exponential delay and jitter, and stop at a budget.
- [Reverse proxy](patterns/reverse-proxy.md): A proxy in front of the origin terminates client connections and can cache, compress, and hide the origin.
- [Saga](patterns/saga.md): Complete a business transaction as a series of local commits with explicit compensations.
- [Sharding](patterns/sharding.md): Split one dataset so each node holds a subset of the keys, usually by hash or by range.
- [Shuffle sharding](patterns/shuffle-sharding.md): Assign each tenant a small random subset of a shared fleet so two tenants rarely share the exact same fate.
- [Sidecar and service mesh](patterns/sidecar-service-mesh.md): Run a helper beside each instance, or a node-level proxy plus optional waypoints, when many services need the same mTLS and traffic policy.
- [Strangler fig](patterns/strangler-fig.md): Route capabilities one at a time from a legacy system to a new one behind a stable facade, then delete the old path.
- [Transactional outbox](patterns/transactional-outbox.md): Commit the business write and the outbound message in one database transaction, then publish asynchronously.
- [Write-behind](patterns/write-behind.md): The application writes the cache and the store is updated asynchronously after the caller has been told success.
- [Write-through](patterns/write-through.md): The application writes the cache and the cache writes the store before the write returns.

## Templates

- [Templates](templates/README.md): Copyable templates for a design doc, an ADR, an RFC, a threat model, an SLO, a runbook, a postmortem, a capacity worksheet, a vendor evaluation, a production-readiness review, and a DPIA.
- [ADR template pointer](templates/adr.md): The canonical Architecture Decision Record template lives with the adr-writer skill. Copy that file, not a second variant.
- [Capacity estimate worksheet](templates/capacity-estimate.md): A worksheet for request rate, bandwidth, storage, the first bottleneck, and the cost driver.
- [Design doc template](templates/design-doc.md): Outline for a system design with requirements, estimates, a component sketch, data, API, and tradeoffs.
- [DPIA template](templates/dpia.md): A Data Protection Impact Assessment outline aligned to GDPR Article 35: processing description, necessity, risks to people, and measures.
- [Postmortem template](templates/postmortem.md): A blameless incident write-up with a timeline, impact, contributing factors, and owned actions.
- [Production readiness review template](templates/production-readiness-review.md): A launch checklist with an evidence column and a gate per service tier, covering ownership, SLOs, failure, security, data, rollout, cost, and audit.
- [RFC template](templates/rfc.md): Outline for a proposal several teams still have to critique: problem, goals, the proposal, alternatives, risks, rollout, and who decides.
- [Runbook template](templates/runbook.md): The steps on-call follows for one page, including how to tell that the mitigation worked.
- [SLO template](templates/slo.md): A one-page definition of an SLI, its target and window, and what happens when the error budget burns.
- [Threat model template](templates/threat-model.md): A STRIDE worksheet tied to the trust boundaries of one design.
- [Vendor evaluation template](templates/vendor-evaluation.md): A scored comparison of build, buy, or adopt: requirements, weights, security questions, a three-year cost, and how you leave.

## Examples

- [Worked example: multi-tenant audit log](pack/examples/multi-tenant-audit-log/README.md): A hand-run of the architect and design-reviewer skills on one multi-tenant audit log, including where the review disagrees with the design.
- [Multi-tenant audit log design](pack/examples/multi-tenant-audit-log/design.md): Architect-skill design for a multi-tenant audit log, covering ingest, tenant-scoped search, export, retention, and the capacity arithmetic.
- [Multi-tenant audit log review](pack/examples/multi-tenant-audit-log/review.md): Design-reviewer findings on the multi-tenant audit log, led by the missing erasure path and the single-writer hash chain.
